review: 1:1–1:2 עֻזֵּנוּ … נִשְׂבָּעָה — Psalm 46:2 (עֹז) with Ps 16:11 and Eph 3:19 (תִּמָּלְאוּ); the Arabic عِزُّنَا … نَشْبَعُ is that pair, and עֹז is the psalm's noun for strength.

1:3–1:4 וְכָל־עֹז בִּלְעָדָיו / אָכֵן יִנָּטֵל — the Arabic وَكُلُّ عِزٍّ غَيْرَهُ / لَا بُدَّ يُنْزَعُ is 'every might besides Him must be taken away'; נָטַל in the niphal is the biblical verb for being lifted off (Isa 33:20 of a tent taken down).

2:3–2:4 נָחַלְנוּ חֶבֶר / וְלָנוּ בּוֹ יִתְרוֹן — the Arabic نِلْنَا شِرْكَةً / لَنَا بِهَا امْتِيَاز is 'we obtained a fellowship, and in it a distinction'; חֶבֶר is the biblical noun for a company joined together (Ps 119:63), and יִתְרוֹן is Qoheleth's word for advantage.

3:1–3:2 לוּ נִשְׂבַּע בּוֹ / וְנִשְׁתַּדֵּל — the Arabic يَا لَيْتَ بِهِ نَقْنَعُ / وَنَسْعَى is an optative; לוּ with the imperfect is the biblical way to say 'would that we…', and שָׁקַד/שָׁדַל in the hithpa'el carries the striving.

4:3 נַבִּיט בּוֹ עֲטוּר — Revelation 19:12 and Heb 2:9 (בְּכָבוֹד וְהָדָר תְּעַטְּרֵהוּ); the Arabic نَنْظُرُهُ مُكَلَّلًا / بِالْمَجْدِ وَالْجَلَال is that crowning, and the Hebrew keeps the participle with the two nouns on the next line.
